country.name: Czechia
country.tagline: Moravian cellar lanes, Pálava limestone and the Elbe hills of Bohemia: a wine culture older than the country's beer fame suggests.

stats.note: No current official area found this session; Wikipedia (de) gives about 18,750 ha for 2004. Moravia holds about 94 to 96 percent. OIV estimates Czech consumption at 2.0 mhl in 2025, far above domestic output.

country.overview:
Czechia is famous for beer, but South Moravia is one of central Europe's liveliest wine regions, and its villages are lined with sklepy, rows of small cellars dug into loess where families make and pour their own wine. The country has two wine regions: Morava (Moravia), with about 95 percent of the vineyard, in the warm south-east bordering Austria and Slovakia, and Čechy (Bohemia), a tiny but historic area along the Elbe and Vltava north of Prague around Mělník and Litoměřice.

Moravia's four subregions (Znojemská, Mikulovská, Velkopavlovická and Slovácká) continue the landscapes of Austria's Weinviertel across the border, and the grapes overlap: Grüner Veltliner (Veltlínské zelené), Welschriesling (Ryzlink vlašský), Riesling (Ryzlink rýnský), Müller-Thurgau, Sauvignon Blanc, the Pinot family, Pálava and Gewürztraminer among whites; Saint Laurent (Svatovavřinecké), Blaufränkisch (Frankovka), Zweigelt, Pinot Noir (Rulandské modré) and Czech crossings such as André and Cabernet Moravia among reds. The best wines are fresh, aromatic whites with lively acidity, and an active natural-wine scene, centred on growers of the Autentista group around Mikulov and Velké Pavlovice, has given Moravia an international following.

Czech wine law follows the EU model, with the German-style Prädikat ladder for quality wines, but its most interesting feature is the VOC (víno originální certifikace, 'wine of original certification'), a local appellation run by growers' associations that sets grapes and style for a named area. VOC Znojmo was first in 2009, and by 2019 there were 13. Valtice Castle, part of the Lednice-Valtice UNESCO landscape, houses the national Wine Salon, which each year selects the country's 100 best wines.

history.title: Roman legions on the Dyje
history.text: Roman legions campaigned and camped at Mušov (Burgstall) below the Pálava hills during the Marcomannic Wars; local tradition credits Roman soldiers with the first Moravian vines, though hard evidence is debated.

history.title: Ludmila's vineyards at Mělník
history.text: Legend says Prince Bořivoj and his wife Ludmila planted the first Bohemian vineyards around Mělník; Ludmila, later Bohemia's patron saint, is honoured by the town's wine.

history.title: Charles IV's vineyards
history.text: Emperor Charles IV encouraged planting around Prague with land grants and tax relief and restricted imports; the Prague district of Vinohrady ('vineyards') recalls the era. The 14th to 16th centuries were Bohemian and Moravian wine's golden age.

history.title: Thirty Years' War
history.text: Before the war Bohemia had an estimated 10,000 ha and Moravia 20,000 ha of vines; destruction and the rise of beer shrank both dramatically.

history.title: Valtice wine school
history.text: A wine school was founded at Valtice, the Liechtenstein seat whose vineyards appear in a register of 1414.

history.title: The VOC system
history.text: VOC Znojmo (2009) became the first wine of original certification; 12 more followed by 2019.

country.classification:
Czech wine follows EU categories: víno (wine), zemské víno (PGI, from the České or Moravské regions), jakostní víno (quality wine from a region or subregion) and jakostní víno s přívlastkem (Prädikat wine: kabinetní víno, pozdní sběr, výběr z hroznů, výběr z bobulí, výběr z cibéb, ledové víno and slámové víno), defined by sugar at harvest. The EU register holds Čechy and Morava, the six subregions, and three local PDOs: Znojmo (the VOC), Šobes and Novosedelské Slámové víno.

VOC (víno originální certifikace) is a growers' appellation for a defined area, with its own varieties, styles and tasting control, closer to the Austrian DAC than to the Prädikat system. The 13 VOCs are Znojmo (2009), Mikulov and Modré Hory (2011), Pálava (2012), Blatnice (2013), Valtice and Mělník (2015), Slovácko and Hustopečsko (2016), Kraví hora and Bzenec (2017), Mutěnice (2018) and Velké Pavlovice (2019).
country.climate_soils: Moravia has a warm continental climate on the edge of the Pannonian basin, with hot summers, cold winters and modest rainfall; loess dominates, with Jurassic limestone on the Pálava hills, granite and gneiss around Znojmo and the Dyje valley, and sand and flysch in Slovácko. Bohemia is cooler, with vineyards on sheltered south-facing slopes over the Elbe and Vltava on sandstone, marl and basalt (around Velké Žernoseky).

grapes.name: Grüner Veltliner (Veltlínské zelené)
grapes.note: Leading white in Znojmo and Mikulov.

grapes.name: Welschriesling (Ryzlink vlašský)
grapes.note: Classic in Mikulov and Velké Pavlovice.

grapes.name: Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay
Pálava
grapes.note: A Czech crossing of Gewürztraminer and Müller-Thurgau, aromatic and often off-dry.

grapes.name: Blaufränkisch (Frankovka), Zweigelt, Pinot Noir
grapes.note: Main reds of Velkopavlovická and Slovácko.

regions.name: Morava
regions.tagline: South Moravia: cellar lanes, loess and Pálava limestone on the Austrian border.
regions.summary: Moravia holds about 95 percent of Czech vineyards in four subregions along the Austrian and Slovak borders. The largest wine villages are Velké Bílovice (766 ha), Valtice (578 ha), Mikulov (516 ha) and Čejkovice (515 ha). Fresh, aromatic whites dominate, with reds in Velkopavlovická and Slovácko.
regions.history: Roman, Great Moravian and monastic roots; the Liechtensteins of Valtice and Lednice and the Dietrichsteins of Mikulov shaped the landscape. Communism nationalised the industry; since 1989 family wineries and cellar villages have revived it.
regions.terroir: Loess, limestone (Pálava), granite and gneiss (Znojmo), sand and flysch (Slovácko); warm continental climate.
regions.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling, Müller-Thurgau, Riesling, Pálava, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot varieties, Saint Laurent, Blaufränkisch, Zweigelt.
regions.styles: Dry and off-dry whites, Prädikat wines, reds, rosé, sparkling, straw and ice wine.
regions.classification: PDO Morava with subregions Znojemská, Mikulovská, Velkopavlovická and Slovácká, plus VOCs.

regions.name: Čechy
regions.tagline: A sliver of vines on the Elbe, where Czech wine began in legend.
regions.summary: Bohemia has only about 4 to 5 percent of Czech vineyards, in the Mělnická and Litoměřická subregions on the Elbe and Vltava north of Prague, plus small plots in Prague itself and around Most. Müller-Thurgau, Riesling and Saint Laurent lead, and Mělník's château winery and the old cellars of Velké Žernoseky are the landmarks.
regions.history: Ludmila's legendary planting at Mělník and Charles IV's support for vineyards around Prague in the fourteenth century.
regions.terroir: Sandstone, marl and basalt on south-facing river slopes; cooler and drier than Moravia.
regions.grapes: Müller-Thurgau, Riesling, Saint Laurent, Pinot Noir, Pinot Blanc, Gewürztraminer.
regions.classification: PDO Čechy with subregions Mělnická and Litoměřická; VOC Mělník.

cz-blatnice.name: Blatnice
cz-blatnice.summary: VOC for Blatnice pod Svatým Antonínkem and nearby villages in Slovácko, best known for a traditional white blend. Like all VOCs it is run by a local growers' association that fixes varieties, style and a tasting check; it sits inside the subregion PDO rather than having its own EU registration.

cz-bzenec.name: Bzenec
cz-bzenec.summary: VOC for Bzenec, whose sandy soils have long been famous for Riesling (Ryzlink rýnský). Like all VOCs it is run by a local growers' association that fixes varieties, style and a tasting check; it sits inside the subregion PDO rather than having its own EU registration.

cz-cechy.name: Čechy
cz-cechy.grapes: Müller-Thurgau, Riesling, Saint Laurent, Pinot Noir
cz-cechy.summary: The regional PDO for Bohemia's small vineyards, covering 67 municipalities in the EU register along the Elbe, Vltava and Ohře and in Prague.

cz-hustopecsko.name: Hustopečsko
cz-hustopecsko.summary: VOC for the area around Hustopeče, a town of almond orchards and wine. Like all VOCs it is run by a local growers' association that fixes varieties, style and a tasting check; it sits inside the subregion PDO rather than having its own EU registration.

cz-kravi-hora.name: Kraví hora
cz-kravi-hora.summary: VOC for the Kraví hora hill at Bořetice, a sunny loess and sandstone slope with a famous cellar village and lookout tower. Like all VOCs it is run by a local growers' association that fixes varieties, style and a tasting check; it sits inside the subregion PDO rather than having its own EU registration.

cz-litomericka.name: Litoměřická
cz-litomericka.grapes: Müller-Thurgau, Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Blanc, Saint Laurent
cz-litomericka.summary: The northern Bohemian subregion along the Elbe around Litoměřice, Velké Žernoseky, Roudnice nad Labem and Most, in the volcanic landscape of the České středohoří hills. Velké Žernoseky's deep cellars are among the oldest wine cellars in Bohemia.
cz-litomericka.terroir: Basalt, volcanic tuff, sandstone and marl on Elbe slopes.

cz-melnicka.name: Mělnická
cz-melnicka.grapes: Müller-Thurgau, Riesling, Pinot Noir, Saint Laurent, Pinot Blanc
cz-melnicka.summary: The subregion around Mělník at the confluence of the Elbe and Vltava, including Prague's historic vineyards. Mělník's Lobkowicz château winery and its terraced slopes above the rivers are the emblem of Bohemian wine, linked to St. Ludmila and Charles IV.
cz-melnicka.terroir: Sandstone and marl slopes at the river confluence.
cz-melnicka.nerd_note: Tradition credits Charles IV with bringing Burgundian vines to Mělník; Pinot Noir is still a local speciality.

cz-melnik.name: Mělník
cz-melnik.summary: Bohemia's only VOC, for the historic vineyards around Mělník on the Elbe and Vltava. Like all VOCs it is run by a local growers' association that fixes varieties, style and a tasting check; it sits inside the subregion PDO rather than having its own EU registration.

cz-mikulov.name: Mikulov
cz-mikulov.summary: VOC for the area around Mikulov and the Pálava hills, focused on dry whites such as Welschriesling, Grüner Veltliner, Riesling and the Pinots. Like all VOCs it is run by a local growers' association that fixes varieties, style and a tasting check; it sits inside the subregion PDO rather than having its own EU registration.

cz-mikulovska.name: Mikulovská
cz-mikulovska.grapes: Welschriesling, Grüner Veltliner, Riesling, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay, Pálava
cz-mikulovska.summary: Mikulovská surrounds the Pálava hills, a limestone ridge rising sharply from the plain south of Brno, with the towns of Mikulov and Valtice and villages such as Dolní Dunajovice, Pavlov and Novosedly. Its Jurassic limestone and loess give the most structured Czech whites, especially Welschriesling, Riesling and Pinot Gris. The subregion is also the centre of Moravia's natural-wine movement.
cz-mikulovska.terroir: Jurassic limestone of the Pálava hills, loess and sand; warm and dry.
cz-mikulovska.nerd_note: The Pálava hills are a UNESCO biosphere reserve whose rare steppe flora grows between the vines.

cz-modre-hory.name: Modré Hory
cz-modre-hory.summary: 'Blue Mountains', a VOC for red wines from villages around Bořetice, Kobylí, Němčičky and Velké Pavlovice, with Frankovka, Saint Laurent, Zweigelt and Portugieser. Like all VOCs it is run by a local growers' association that fixes varieties, style and a tasting check; it sits inside the subregion PDO rather than having its own EU registration.

cz-morava.name: Morava
cz-morava.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling, Müller-Thurgau, Riesling, Saint Laurent, Blaufränkisch and many others
cz-morava.summary: The regional PDO for Moravia, covering 301 municipalities in the EU register and about 95 percent of Czech vineyards. It is used for quality and Prädikat wine from anywhere in the four Moravian subregions.

cz-mutenice.name: Mutěnice
cz-mutenice.summary: VOC for Mutěnice, a large wine village with a viticulture research station and cellar lanes. Like all VOCs it is run by a local growers' association that fixes varieties, style and a tasting check; it sits inside the subregion PDO rather than having its own EU registration.

cz-novosedelske-slamove-vino.name: Novosedelské Slámové víno
cz-novosedelske-slamove-vino.summary: A PDO for straw wine (slámové víno) from the village of Novosedly near Mikulov, made from grapes dried on straw or hung for months before pressing, giving intensely sweet wines. Novosedly is one of the largest wine villages in Moravia (about 421 ha).
cz-novosedelske-slamove-vino.terroir: Loess and sand below the Pálava hills.
cz-novosedelske-slamove-vino.nerd_note: One of very few straw-wine PDOs in Europe.

cz-palava.name: Pálava
cz-palava.summary: VOC for wines from the villages around the Pálava limestone ridge (Pavlov, Dolní Věstonice, Perná, Bavory, Klentnice), known for structured whites. Like all VOCs it is run by a local growers' association that fixes varieties, style and a tasting check; it sits inside the subregion PDO rather than having its own EU registration.

cz-slovacka.name: Slovácká
cz-slovacka.grapes: Riesling, Welschriesling, Müller-Thurgau, Grüner Veltliner, Saint Laurent, Blaufränkisch
cz-slovacka.summary: The eastern Moravian subregion (Moravian Slovakia), around Mutěnice, Bzenec, Strážnice, Blatnice and Uherské Hradiště, a folk-culture landscape of painted cellars and wine festivals. Sandy soils at Bzenec give famous Riesling, and the slopes of the White Carpathians near Blatnice give fresh whites.
cz-slovacka.terroir: Sand, loess and Carpathian flysch; slightly wetter and cooler near the hills.
cz-slovacka.nerd_note: Blatnice's St. Anthony chapel on its hill is a pilgrimage site above the vines.

cz-slovacko.name: Slovácko
cz-slovacko.summary: VOC for wines from the Slovácko subregion's villages, emphasising local character. Like all VOCs it is run by a local growers' association that fixes varieties, style and a tasting check; it sits inside the subregion PDO rather than having its own EU registration.

cz-sobes.name: Šobes / Šobeské víno
cz-sobes.grapes: Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc, Grüner Veltliner, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Welschriesling, Pálava, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Noir
cz-sobes.summary: Šobes is a single vineyard of about 13 hectares on a south-facing slope inside a meander of the Dyje river in the Podyjí National Park near Znojmo, reachable by foot or boat. Often called one of the oldest vineyards in central Europe, it has its own EU PDO (2011) and gives fine Riesling and Sauvignon from gneiss and granite.
cz-sobes.terroir: Weathered gneiss and granite on a sun-trap slope enclosed by the river canyon.
cz-sobes.nerd_note: The vineyard lies opposite the Austrian Thayatal National Park across the river.

cz-valtice.name: Valtice
cz-valtice.summary: VOC for the Valtice area, seat of the Liechtenstein château and the National Wine Salon. Like all VOCs it is run by a local growers' association that fixes varieties, style and a tasting check; it sits inside the subregion PDO rather than having its own EU registration.

cz-velke-pavlovice.name: Velké Pavlovice
cz-velke-pavlovice.summary: VOC for Velké Pavlovice, the red-wine and apricot town of central Moravia. Like all VOCs it is run by a local growers' association that fixes varieties, style and a tasting check; it sits inside the subregion PDO rather than having its own EU registration.

cz-velkopavlovicka.name: Velkopavlovická
cz-velkopavlovicka.grapes: Blaufränkisch, Saint Laurent, Zweigelt, André, Pinot Noir, Welschriesling, Grüner Veltliner
cz-velkopavlovicka.summary: The central Moravian subregion around Velké Pavlovice, Velké Bílovice (the largest wine village in the country, about 766 ha), Hustopeče, Čejkovice, Bořetice and Kobylí. Rolling loess hills with apricot orchards make it the red-wine heart of Czechia, home of Frankovka, Saint Laurent and the André crossing, bred here in 1961.
cz-velkopavlovicka.terroir: Deep loess, sand and marl on rolling hills; warm summers.
cz-velkopavlovicka.nerd_note: The red crossing André (Blaufränkisch x Saint Laurent) was bred in this part of Moravia and remains a local favourite.

cz-znojemska.name: Znojemská
cz-znojemska.grapes: Grüner Veltliner, Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling, Müller-Thurgau, Pinot Blanc
cz-znojemska.summary: The western Moravian subregion around Znojmo on the Dyje (Thaya), facing Austria's Weinviertel across the border. Granite and gneiss in the Dyje canyon and loess elsewhere give aromatic, crisp whites, especially Grüner Veltliner, Sauvignon Blanc and Riesling. It includes the Šobes vineyard and the villages of Hnanice, Nový Šaldorf, Vrbovec (344 ha) and Dobšice.
cz-znojemska.terroir: Granite, gneiss and loess; the coolest and most aromatic of the Moravian subregions.
cz-znojemska.nerd_note: Znojmo's medieval underground labyrinth was used for wine storage.

cz-znojmo.name: Znojmo
cz-znojmo.summary: The first Czech VOC (2009) and the only one registered separately as an EU PDO (2011). It covers 22 villages around Znojmo and allows only Veltlínské zelené, Ryzlink rýnský and Sauvignon, in a fresh, aromatic dry style. The Znojmo growers' initiative became the model for later VOCs.
cz-znojmo.terroir: Granite, gneiss and loess in the Dyje valley.
cz-znojmo.nerd_note: The EU register caps VOC Znojmo at 12,000 kg of grapes per hectare.

sites.name: Valtice Château and Salon vín
sites.class: National Wine Salon in the Liechtenstein château cellars
sites.text: The baroque château of the Liechtensteins at Valtice, part of the Lednice-Valtice Cultural Landscape (UNESCO, 1996), houses in its cellars the Salon vín České republiky, which each year presents the 100 best Czech wines chosen in a national competition. Valtice also had a wine school from 1873.

sites.name: Mikulov Castle
sites.text: The Dietrichstein château towering over Mikulov houses the regional museum and a giant wine barrel built in 1643, one of the largest in central Europe.

sites.name: Svatý kopeček, Mikulov
sites.text: A limestone hill with a Way of the Cross and chapel above Mikulov's vineyards, with views over the Pálava and the Austrian border.

sites.name: Děvín (Pálava hills)
sites.class: Highest point of the Pálava, UNESCO biosphere reserve
sites.text: The 549-metre summit of the Pálava hills, a Jurassic limestone ridge whose southern slopes are planted with vines among protected steppe grassland.

sites.name: Vinařství Sonberk
sites.text: A modern winery on the Sonberk hill at Popice, overlooking the Nové Mlýny reservoirs and the Pálava, known for Riesling and Pálava.

sites.name: Kraví hora, Bořetice
sites.class: VOC Kraví hora cellar village and lookout
sites.text: A sunny hill above Bořetice with rows of wine cellars, a lookout tower and vineyards on loess and sandstone, now its own VOC.

sites.name: Šobes vineyard
sites.text: A sun-trap slope in a meander of the Dyje in the Podyjí National Park, one of the oldest vineyards in central Europe and its own PDO.

sites.name: Znojmo
sites.text: A historic town on a cliff above the Dyje, with an underground labyrinth once used for wine, an annual historic harvest festival and the first Czech VOC.

sites.name: Novosedly
sites.text: A large wine village west of Mikulov, the only village with its own straw-wine PDO.

sites.name: Mělník Château (Lobkowicz)
sites.class: Historic château winery at the Elbe-Vltava confluence
sites.text: The Lobkowicz château on a cliff above the meeting of the Vltava and the Elbe, with terraced vineyards below and cellars that are the symbol of Bohemian wine.

sites.name: Grébovka (Prague Vinohrady)
sites.text: A restored vineyard and pavilion in the Havlíčkovy sady park in the Prague district of Vinohrady, named after the vineyards Charles IV encouraged around the city.
